beats.say: Early Unix was available through inexpensive source-code licenses, because a 1956 antitrust settlement kept AT&T out of the commercial computer business.
But AT&T's breakup in 1984 opened the way to sell Unix commercially, and it abruptly raised the price from 99 dollars to 250,000 dollars.
Berkeley released its networking code as Net/1 in June 1989, and a completely free BSD Unix finally shipped in June 1991.
